title: Size limits: decimal precision 38; strings 4 GiB - 1 (panic past it); rows 2^32 - 1 by default
verdict: Decimal: at most 38 digits; a string or binary over u32::MAX bytes panics; the default runtime caps a frame at 2^32 - 1 rows
description: `Decimal` is a 128-bit type with at most 38 digits of precision (also the default when the precision is not given) and a non-negative scale. The page does not say what an overflow does; Polars's tests pin that it raises `ComputeError: overflow in decimal …`.

Source at py-2.1.0: strings and binaries are binary views whose `length` is a `u32`. The builder asserts `bytes.len() <= u32::MAX` (`push_value_into_buffer`), so a longer value panics (a `PanicException` in Python) where it would be an error elsewhere. Lists are `ListArray<i64>`, with 64-bit offsets checked on push (`Offsets::try_push` returns an `overflow` error). Row indices are `IdxSize`, a `u32` in the default `polars-runtime-32` that `pip install polars` brings; `polars[rt64]` switches to `u64` (`bigidx`). Past 2^32 - 1 rows the default runtime reports "Polars' maximum length reached. Consider installing 'polars[rt64]'.", as an error at most sites and a panic at some (`expect(LENGTH_LIMIT_MSG)`).
Leads: py-polars/tests/unit/datatypes/test_decimal.py for decimal overflow (polars-decimal-arith covers arithmetic).
The docs are silent on the `u32` string length and the `u32` row limit of the default runtime: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins a string over `u32::MAX` bytes or a list offset overflow; it may change between versions.
reference: The reference caps decimals at 38 digits and raises past them; it has no limit on string, blob or list lengths.

evidence.note: View: u32 length, buffer index and offset
one data buffer holds at most i32::MAX bytes
rt64 and rtcompat turn on bigidx
polars depends on polars-runtime-32; rt64 is an extra
Decimal(38, 0) +, -, * past 38 digits raise ComputeError 'overflow in decimal' (eager)
`test_decimal_sum_overflow_28585`, streaming and in-memory: sum overflow raises
row count 2^32 raises ComputeError with the rt64 hint (default runtime). No test of over-long strings or list offset overflow
